recognition: I recognize this as the UCI Online Shoppers Purchasing Intention dataset, a familiar session-level conversion classification benchmark. That recognition and its supplied metadata are not discoveries. Revenue is observed per session; the bundle does not provide event timing or an intervention.

candidates.title: Is PageValues a label-proximal measurement channel?
candidates.question: How much of the apparent session-level association with Revenue depends on PageValues, compared with the other recorded session features?

core.object: Revenue classification from the supplied session features
core.relation_or_action: Compare held-out performance and calibration for a model using PageValues alone, all features, and all features except PageValues
core.contrast: PageValues included versus excluded, with identical session-level splits and modeling procedure
core.prediction: Including PageValues will substantially improve held-out performance over the model without it; if the no-PageValues model performs similarly, PageValues is not the main source of predictive signal in this dataset.
core.independent_unit: Session, as represented by one row

candidates.failure_condition: The prediction fails if excluding PageValues does not produce a material, uncertainty-supported decline in held-out performance relative to the full-feature model.
assumptions: The supplied rows and labels are accurately represented.
The fixed dataset split and evaluation procedure avoid tuning on held-out results.
Predictive dependence does not establish that PageValues causes conversion or is available before conversion.
candidates.domain_value: Tests whether reported conversion prediction relies on a metric whose documentation ties it to pages visited before a transaction, helping distinguish potentially actionable session signals from a label-proximal metric.
candidates.discriminating_delta: Quantifies the incremental predictive contribution of PageValues against both a PageValues-only reference and the other recorded features, rather than proposing another generic conversion predictor.

candidates.title: Does visitor type mark different conversion correlates?
candidates.question: Among sessions with similar recorded engagement and traffic characteristics, does the association between product-page engagement and Revenue differ for New_Visitor and Returning_Visitor sessions?

core.object: Revenue and ProductRelated_Duration across VisitorType groups
core.relation_or_action: Estimate whether the conditional association between ProductRelated_Duration and Revenue varies by VisitorType
core.contrast: New_Visitor versus Returning_Visitor sessions, adjusting for the other supplied session features and Month
core.prediction: The engagement-Revenue association will differ between new and returning visitors after adjustment.
core.independent_unit: Session, as represented by one row

candidates.failure_condition: The prediction fails if the estimated interaction is small or uncertain under a prespecified model and sensitivity checks.
assumptions: The visitor-type categories are consistently recorded.
Sessions are the analysis units; no user-level repeated measurements are represented in the bundle.
Adjustment cannot eliminate unmeasured confounding or establish an intervention effect.
candidates.domain_value: Could identify whether session-level engagement has different descriptive relevance across visitor groups, informing what subgroup-specific follow-up data would be useful.
candidates.discriminating_delta: Tests a prespecified interaction in an observed relationship instead of asking whether visitor type or engagement predicts conversion in general.

candidates.title: Are month-level conversion differences compositional?
candidates.question: How much of the observed variation in Revenue across Month remains after standardizing months to a common distribution of VisitorType and TrafficType?

core.relation_or_action: Compare observed monthly rates with rates standardized to a shared VisitorType and TrafficType distribution
core.contrast: Raw month-specific rates versus composition-standardized rates
core.prediction: Standardization will reduce at least part of the between-month variation if visitor and traffic composition accounts for some of it.
core.independent_unit: Session, with uncertainty estimated to reflect session counts within months

candidates.failure_condition: The prediction fails if standardized rates show no meaningful reduction in between-month variation, or uncertainty makes the reduction indistinguishable from zero.
assumptions: Month and group labels are recorded consistently.
The available categories permit standardization without relying on unsupported extrapolation.
Standardization is descriptive and does not identify causal seasonal effects.
candidates.domain_value: Separates a descriptive seasonal pattern from differences in the observed mix of visitors and traffic sources, guiding whether further calendar or campaign data are needed.
candidates.discriminating_delta: Makes a specific composition-based comparison rather than treating raw monthly conversion variation as a seasonal mechanism.

selection_reason: Under the supplied lexicographic rule, all three candidates pass the self-reported quality gates, have the same no-history relation, and are feasible with current data. The lowest candidate index therefore selects I1. This is a forecast from the rule, not an evaluation result.

task.deliverable: Evaluate the prespecified held-out comparison of PageValues-only, full-feature, and no-PageValues models on the supplied session rows; report performance differences with uncertainty and the split/model details.
task.acceptance: Use the same session-level split and evaluation procedure across comparisons; disclose the dataset recognition; report actual results rather than treating feasibility or metadata as confirmation. Interpret results as observational prediction evidence, not causal or real-time actionability. If PageValues materially contributes, identify its documented measurement meaning and state that event-timing data would be needed to establish availability at a decision point.
